holding_summary: A boarding house keeper contracted to furnish board and lodging to 45 convention delegates through a committee treasurer, who failed to have the guests occupy the agreed accommodations. The court held the contract enforceable but that damages for the breach were limited to the keeper's actual loss, not the full agreed price. Judgment for the boarding house keeper was reversed solely on the measure-of-damages instruction.

quotes.text: The plaintiff, a boarding house keeper, agreed to furnish board and lodging to 45 persons, to be sent to her house by the committee of the Eleventh International Christian Endeavor Convention, of which the defendant was treasurer.
The claim seems to be a meritorious one, and ought to be discharged in a practical manner, by its payment.

The true measure of damages by a boarding house keeper against those engaging board and lodging, and not taking the agreed accommodations, is not what the parties agreed to pay, but.what the plaintiff lost in consequence of the breach.

notes: Court treats the boarding-house/lodging contract as an ordinary commercial arrangement enforceable at law; duration of the intended occupancy is not stated in the opinion beyond the convention context, so left unclear.
